precepts.text: Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments. Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers. Why? Because we would forget who we are; we would lose our way; and he is going to turn us back to our forefathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
precepts.point: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in. Now, you may think initially it is talking about John the Baptist; that is a good thought, but it is actually talking about the John the Baptist work in the last days.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
“Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me”. You may think at first that is only John the Baptist. That is a good thought, but it is the John the Baptist work in the last days, and the end of Malachi shows it.

“Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” Then here it comes: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”. That is still the John the Baptist work, but in the last days it is Elijah, sent before that great and dreadful day.

What would he do? “And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children”. Why? Because we would forget who we are. We would lose our way. “And the heart of the children to their fathers”: he is going to show us our forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and turn us back to them, “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

So the messenger of Malachi 3 is the messenger sent before the Lord comes to his temple in the last days, to bring a people who forgot themselves back to their fathers and their law before the day of his coming.

precepts.text: Learn a parable of the fig tree: when his branch is tender and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh; so likewise, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors. The destruction is at the doors, and here we are playing games.
precepts.point: We set up programs to protect you, sisters and brothers, because we have a vantage point over you: you are upset you cannot move as fast as you want, but the brother is not ready to prove that sister and the sister needs to work on herself. Fathers see the landscape of the whole congregation and can tell when a brother is not in his right mind while the daughter sees only that he is cute. Lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
“Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh”. Christ is saying, pay attention to the seasons. Watch the fig tree; when the branches are tender and the leaves come out, you know summer is near by how the trees are changing.

“So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” We do not know the day and we do not know the hour, but we know we are in the season. The prophets wrote down what was coming, and now we actually see it: the missiles sitting in the silos ready to rock, the mushroom cloud Isaiah 34 speaks of. They did not have that when Malachi brought this out, but it is here now, letting us know what time we are in. You are not going to get a bigger sign than that.

So that is where we are: the destruction is even at the doors, and here we are playing games. That is what Malachi was saying: “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.” Smite the earth with destruction. So we had better remember the law of Moses, the laws and the commandments, and keep them, so that we are not caught off guard when that day comes. Knowing these things are coming, our minds and our spirits need to be right.

precepts.text: What shall be the parting asunder of the times, or when shall be the end of the first and the beginning of it that followeth? From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau, for Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. The only clue given, and the churches do not even know who Esau is. The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: the other nations are between, insignificant, affected by one or the other, and they will never rule. Bishop Nathanyel's class on the Achilles heel goes with this like cookies and milk.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
Ezra is still dealing with the mind of God. The Lord had said all things “were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” That is the smiting of the earth with a curse. We cannot move God's timetable; not a sparrow falls without the Father, and he has millions of things lined up that we are not even aware of. You are trying to move God with your hastiness, and yet you will not even keep the commandments.

Then Ezra asks for the sign: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” When shall this wicked rule end? It is the same question the disciples asked in Matthew 24: when shall these things be?

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” That is the only clue given, and the people in the churches do not even know who Esau is, so they are completely lost. Bishop Nathanyel's class on the Achilles heel goes with this like cookies and milk.

“For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Once we find out who Esau is, see how he is acting on this earth and read about him in the Bible, we know the time is near, even at the doors. And Jacob is the beginning of what follows: Jacob is going to rule; that is the kingdom. Seeing all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought we to be? Our minds need to be on that level.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”. The other nations are in between, insignificant, affected by one or the other, and they will never rule.

precepts.text: The great dragon was cast out, the red dragon, Esau, the Roman Empire that entered our heaven and cast us into captivity; the heaven he falls from is his rulership now, not some fight at creation, because Satan obeys the Lord, asking permission over Job's hedge and sent as a lying spirit to Ahab's prophets in Kings. That old serpent, back to Cain and Eve, called the Devil, evil, and Satan, adversary: the red man, never white, which deceiveth the whole world with a Charles Manson Jesus, cast out with his angels, his black preachers and ministers who are imps to destroy our people. Christianity has perfected slavery: in chains we still wanted freedom, but this dope put us so far to sleep we do not want to be free. Then a loud voice: now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, for the accuser of our brethren is cast down. When these devils go down, we rule.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
The same transition of time is written in Revelation. “And the great dragon was cast out”: that is Esau, the red dragon, the Romans. That was the Roman Empire that came into our heaven, meaning our kingdom, destroyed Jerusalem and cast us into captivity. The heaven Esau is going to fall from is his ruling kingdom right now. It is not a fight at creation where Satan got kicked out of heaven; that is a perversion of Isaiah 14.

Satan does what the Most High tells him. In Job the Lord asked Satan where he came from, and Satan could not touch Job because of the hedge around him, which is the hedge we want around us. In Kings, when Ahab was to be persuaded to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead, an evil spirit said he would be a lying spirit in the mouth of his prophets, and the Lord sent him. The Lord has control of everything. Here in Revelation 12 is when Christ destroys these demonic forces.

“That old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan”: going all the way back to Cain, back to Eve. Devil means evil; Satan means adversary. That is the white man; he fits it to a tee. And he has never been white: not nasty white, not beige, not off-white. He is red. Stop lying when you look at him.

“Which deceiveth the whole world”: he made everybody on the planet believe Christ looks like Charles Manson, when the Bible gives a full description of Christ as a black man with woolly hair and feet like brass burned in a furnace. That is great deception.

“He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him”: his missionaries, his black preachers and ministers, imps of Satan to destroy our people. Christianity is the perfection of slavery. In chains, being whipped, we still wanted freedom; but Christianity is the greatest dope of all, and it put us so far to sleep we do not even want to be free. It destroyed us from within.

When the Lord casts this devil down and smashes all that Christian garbage and all those lies, then: “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down”. When these devils go down, we rule. That is Jacob, the beginning of the world that follows.

precepts.text: The day cometh that shall burn as an oven, and all the proud and all that do wickedly shall be stubble. Last time it was water; this time the fire burns the soul and you feel it while you are in it. Pride and wickedness are the fuel, so let whatever you are into go before the fire comes. Sabbath sickness is a slogan for lazy bums.
precepts.point: Brothers who want to give their rank up do not understand the work. The life you used to live died with Christ; now you live his life and do his work. A brother asked how to balance his life: this truth is the balance, and there is no life after it.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
Colossians says, “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom.” Malachi shows how deep that warning really is: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven.” That is why every man and every woman in this truth is warned, and why nobody is played with. Fire is coming for this place. Last time it was water, but the Lord promised that this time it is going to be fire, a fire able to burn the soul, and you feel it while you are in it.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble.” It is their pride and their wickedness that bring the fire on them, so you cannot be prideful. Christ died for your sin; he could have taken you out in that moment, but he gave you grace and mercy. Instead of sitting on your behind, build on the platform of Christ: go out and gather the souls Satan is oppressing, the fatherless and the widow. Brothers who want to give their rank up do not understand the work.

“And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Whatever you are into, it is time to let it go before the fire comes. We fight demons every day, and sometimes it is not that you cannot do a thing; you have to command yourself to do it. Sabbath sickness is a whole slogan for brothers that are lazy bums.

So the life you used to live, the wicked life, died with Christ, giving you a chance before the fire. Now you live his life and do his work. A brother asked how to balance his life: this truth is the balance, and there is no life after it. That is the business we are in, in the classroom, on the radio, on TV and in the street: warning people of the destruction to come, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.

precepts.text: The day cometh that shall burn as an oven; it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
precepts.point: The day that burneth as an oven leaves neither root nor branch. God will end them with the weapon he let them make.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
The Lord said, “I have created the waster to destroy.” What weapon at that time could have been called the waster? Nothing. Zechariah describes it: “Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.” Could anybody then fathom a weapon that did those things? Malachi shows the day it is fulfilled: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”.

The prophets did not know about nuclear weapons and atoms back then. They got these visions and explained them the best they could, and the best way to say it was: the waster. God put it on man to make that instrument, and there will be a day when that plague is fulfilled.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: not just Esau and the other nations, but even rebellious Israel, the ones that do not repent. “And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” When you burn something it leaves ashes, but with this waster nothing remains. They show dramatic images, but the body does not survive that heat; whatever ash there is is blown into the atmosphere. You are totally gone.

And here is the beauty of it: God put it in their spirit to make that thing, and he is going to use that same thing to end them. The weapon they feel gave them their power, authority and respect, he will turn against them.

precepts.text: The day cometh that shall burn as an oven, and shall leave them neither root nor branch.
precepts.point: The truth is the word, and the word says the day cometh that shall burn as an oven.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
This is the word that is the truth: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”. The day is coming that is going to burn like an oven. Nuclear fire is coming to America. What are you going to do about that, and how are you going to survive it?

“and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: burnt up like stubble in that day, unless ye repent. “and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch”. Your children will be cut off too.

Psalm 21 sounds just like it: “Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them. Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.” Neither root nor branch left. And Isaiah 14: “Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers”. The forefathers committed the crime, took the wealth and everything from us, and now the children are left holding the bag: Esau, and not just Esau, Elam, Ishmael and the Hamites, all got wealthy off the backs of the Israelites and had us in slavery one way or the other. The Lord will “cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew”, the same son and nephew, root and branch.

“For they intended evil against thee: they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.” The nations counsel against us, but the Lord takes the crafty in their own craftiness and saves the poor, Israel, from the sword.

precepts.text: The Most High sends the prophet to turn the hearts of the fathers and children, lest He come and smite the earth with a curse; our people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
precepts.point: As Zechariah died he said, The Most High look upon it and require it. He prayed for vengeance on his murderer, and this is scripture; it is right to pray for the downfall of enemies who do much wickedness, even while we pray for the recovery and repentance of our own people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

precepts.why:
“And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.” The Most High sends the prophet to turn the hearts of the fathers and the children, lest he come and smite the earth with a curse. Our people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.

Zechariah the son of Jehoiada was that kind of prophet: “the Spirit of God came upon” him, and he stood above the people and asked, “Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper?” He came to correct the king and turn the people back.

But they “stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the Lord.” The king had him killed for telling him the truth. Joash “remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him, but slew his son.” That is the same spirit our people show today when a laborer brings the medicine and is met with violence.

precepts.text: For behold the day cometh that shall burn as an oven, and all the proud and all that do wickedly shall be stubble; this is the day of the Lord.
precepts.point: Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger; the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath and the fire shall devour them.

note.label: Psalm 21: Victory Through the King and the Enemy Destroyed

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them.” Malachi tells when: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.”

This is the day of the Lord. The day comes that burns as an oven, and all the proud and all that do wickedly are stubble, burned up so that neither root nor branch is left. That is the fiery oven of the Most High's anger, the fire that devours them.

precepts.text: Remember the law of Moses for all Israel; Elijah is sent to turn the heart of the fathers to the children before the great and dreadful day.
precepts.point: When brothers ask "were you there?" or "how you know what color he was?" the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. We are supposed to search the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
The fathers told us what the Most High did in the times of old, and Malachi tells us to hold on to it: “Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” The law is for all Israel. “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”, and Elijah is sent to turn the heart of the fathers to the children before that great and dreadful day.

So the work the fathers told of, the heathen driven out and Israel planted by his right hand and not by our own sword, comes with the law of Moses to be remembered. When brothers ask how we know, this is the answer: remember what was told, and search the scriptures.

precepts.text: The Most High promised to send Elijah before the great day, the spirit that comes in John.
precepts.point: All flesh is grass and its goodliness as the flower of the field; the grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever. It compares our lives to the flowers of the field: we are born, we grow, we die, and go back into the ground, but the word of the Most High is forever.

note.label: Isaiah 40: Comfort My People and the Everlasting God

precepts.why:
“The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.” This goes into the prophecy of John, the spirit of Elijah: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”.

The Most High promised to send Elijah before the great and dreadful day, and that is the spirit that comes in John, the voice crying in the wilderness, with every valley exalted, every mountain and hill made low, and the crooked made straight, so that “the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together”.

precepts.text: I will send you Elijah the prophet, and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children before the great and dreadful day.
precepts.point: Because we now understand who we are and can identify our forefathers in this Bible, it means Elijah has already come and gone.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
“Son of man, hast thou seen this?” He brings the prophet back to the brink of the river, and there are very many trees on the one side and on the other. Malachi says, “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

Elijah's work is to turn the heart of the children to their fathers. Because we now understand who we are and can identify our forefathers in this Bible, our hearts have been turned to our fathers. That means Elijah has already come and gone, before the great and dreadful day.

precepts.text: I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.
precepts.point: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judea, saying repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. He is the messenger the prophets said would go before the Lord, coming in the spirit of Elijah.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
The messenger who goes before the Lord comes in the spirit of Elijah: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

John the Baptist is that Elijah, sent before the Lord, turning hearts by preaching “Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Malachi 3:1 tells of the messenger; Malachi 4:5-6 tells whose spirit he would come in. John fits both, preaching in the wilderness of Judea before Christ came to his temple.

precepts.text: I will send you Elijah the prophet, and he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children.
precepts.point: All the prophets and the law prophesied until John, and if ye will receive it, this is Elias which was for to come.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

precepts.why:
“For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.” Elias was for to come; that is a prophecy, and it is Malachi's.

“Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.” Elijah the prophet is sent before the day of the Lord to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children and the children to their fathers. John came before Christ doing that work, so Christ says, if you will receive it, this is Elias. The law and the prophets prophesied until John because John is where the prophecy of Elijah's coming was met.
